messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert fired — streaming_tail_latency_p99 > 2500ms for /v1/streaming/generate in us-west-2 (rule: streaming_tail_latency_p99_5m)

sre-oncall: saw the alert on the SLO dashboard. p95 ~ 580ms -> 900ms, p99 ~ 3100ms. A few streaming timeouts (chunk level) showing HTTP 504s.

nina.p: confirming logs. Correlation: spikes line up with a surge of mixed-length sessions (short chat + a handful of very long >4k-token sessions). Cont-batcher queue shows some long packing times. KV cache hitrate stable.

raj.k: paging oncall. taking lead for live mitigation. Can someone post the customer impact?

cs-rep: CS report: one enterprise customer (acct: magnitude-ai) reported intermittent streaming stalls on long conversations starting ~12:03 UTC. They saw hangups then eventual HTTP 504s.

emma.s: quick metric dump: queue_length cont-batch +35% at spike, pack_latency p95 jumped to 1.4s, pack_latency p99 ~ 4.6s. Looks like head-of-line blocking where big requests delay batch seal.

eng-lead: flag rollout question: was the new packing heuristic enabled recently? We rolled new fairness scheduling last night.

perf-bot: deploy record: flag batcher.enable_fair_sched set true at 02:10 UTC (canary -> prod ramp)

nina.p: yes that matches — `batcher.enable_fair_sched=true` at 02:10. Hypothesis: fair scheduler is trying to be fair across tenants but for streaming it waits for large seqs leading to packed batches delaying emission.

raj.k: mitigation options: (A) flip flag back to false quickly, (B) clamp max_batch_size for streaming route to reduce waiting, (C) force timed flush lower for streaming. Which one is fastest?

sre-oncall: fastest is clamp/timed-flush since flag rollback touches global scheduler and takes longer to converge. But if flag rollback is simple feature-flag flip we can do both: clamp now + rollback after.

raj.k: ok doing approach B+C immediately. I'll also start flag rollback in parallel (canary then region) if needed.

deploy-bot: action started: patching per-route config for /v1/streaming/* in us-west-2.

raj.k: pushing config patch:
```
PATCH /config/batcher/us-west-2
{
  "route":"/v1/streaming/*",
  "max_batch_size":16,
  "timed_flush_ms":10
}
```

ops-bot: config patch accepted, rollout to 100% in us-west-2 scheduled in 15s.

perf-bot: applying temporary clamp. Also starting tracing snapshot for next 10 minutes.

nina.p: started trace capture. Example trace showing stall:
```
Trace: 0x7a3b
- t=12:02:57 req short queued
- t=12:02:58 req long (5.8k tokens) queued
- batch sealed only at t=12:03:06 when long arrives -> streaming emission delayed 8s
```

sre-oncall: metric update 2m after clamp: p95 dropped from 900ms -> 460ms, p99 from 3100ms -> 1200ms. Error rate trending down.

raj.k: starting rollback of `batcher.enable_fair_sched` in us-west-2 (canary first) to be safe.

deploy-bot: feature flag rollback initiated (canary 10% -> region). ETA ~ 3 minutes for canary validation.

eng-lead: make sure we don't remove clamps until we validate scheduler behavior with mixed-length workload in staging. We need a controlled AB test before re-enabling.

cs-rep: updated customer: we applied mitigations, p99 improving, we'll monitor and update in 30m. They asked for a timeline for root cause — will provide postmortem after RCA.

perf-bot: canary rollback result: no regressions in canary for 2m. Rolling to 100% in region now.

deploy-bot: rollback complete in us-west-2. `batcher.enable_fair_sched=false` confirmed.

nina.p: after rollback + clamp: p95 ~420ms, p99 ~820ms. Pack latency tail reduced. KV-cache unaffected. Streaming chunk latency aligns with batch seal times now.

raj.k: leaving max_batch_size=16 and timed_flush_ms=10 for 20 minutes, then increase to 24 if stable. If any regressions, emergency clamp to 8 (ops runbook).

eng-lead: assign owners: postmortem owner = nina.p, scheduler fix = perf team (emma.s + raj.k), customer comms = cs-rep. Postmortem due EOD.

perf-bot: next steps for repro: create mixedlen arrival generator that mimics production ratio (short:long 85:15) and run both schedulers. Capture p99 pack latency + stream stall count.

nina.p: adding traces and dashboards to incident doc: https://redwood.atlassian/INC-6823456789. Linking flamegraphs and histogram snapshots.

sre-oncall: monitoring for 20m. Will keep paging open during window. If p99 > 1500ms re-escalate.

cs-rep: customer asked to be pinged when p99 < 1000ms for 15 consecutive minutes. I will update ticket when threshold met.

raj.k: quick note: avoid feature-flag blpop on scheduler without staged perf tests for streaming-heavy routes. New fair_sched has good intent but needs route-specific knobs (prefer timed flush on streaming).

eng-lead: agreed — design change: scheduler should consider route hint (streaming vs batch) and prefer time-based sealing for streaming. Add to scheduler backlog and prioritize.

perf-bot: created perf experiment ticket referencing incident, includes expected metrics to validate: pack_latency_p95, p99, stream_stall_count, request_error_rate.

ops-bot: emergency clamp instruction in runbook updated: if pack_latency > 500ms -> clamp to 8 and page scheduler oncall.

sre-oncall: p99 sustained < 900ms for last 10 min, error rate normal. Paging standing down after 20m window.

cs-rep: notified customer update: Partial mitigation in place, monitoring. Postmortem to follow with RCA and timeline.

nina.p: postmortem gist: root cause hypothesis — new fair scheduling would hold batches open trying to balance fairness across tenants which increased wait times when mixed sequence-length arrivals included long sessions; streaming route needs tighter time-based flush policy.

raj.k: follow-ups:
- create AB perf test (perf-bot ticket)
- add route-level scheduler hints
- improve rollout gating for scheduler flags (smaller canary + perf checks)
- follow up with customer and include remediation timeline

eng-lead: thanks all. Handoff complete to postmortem owners. Leaving this thread open until incident doc updated. If stable for 30m auto-close will happen.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigation applied — monitoring for 30m. Auto-close if SLO stable.
